title: A Crocodile Missing Its Snout Tip Gets a Name Inspired by the Great Sphinx
summary:
The Great Sphinx in Giza, Egypt, is famous for its missing nose. Now scientists have named a new species of extinct crocodile whose fossil skull is also missing the tip of its snout.

The species is called Herugavialis cairensis. It is described in a new study in the journal Royal Society Open Science.

The crocodile was a gavial. Gavials are crocodiles with long, thin snouts. Only two species are alive today, and they live in fresh water in India and nearby countries and in Southeast Asia. But fossils show gavials once lived all over the world, often in shallow seas.

In the 1920s, several crocodile fossils, including a nearly complete skull, were dug up from Egypt's 45-million-year-old Mokattam Formation, a layer of rock. Popular Science describes the find as coming from the rocks of the Great Sphinx. At first, scientists thought the skull belonged to a type of crocodile still alive today, called the false gharial, because the two look alike.

Over the past 100 years, new tools have made it easier to look inside fossil skulls. When researchers studied this one again, they found it was a different, new species.

The missing snout tip gave them an idea for the name. "Given this coincidence with the famously missing nose of the Great Sphinx, we decided to name the new crocodile after the Egyptian god Heru," said study co-author Philip Mannion of University College London.

Long ago, the region was covered by shallow seas that held at least two other kinds of gavials. Co-author Paul Burke of the Swedish Museum of Natural History said the number of crocodile kinds around the Mediterranean rose and fell with changes in temperature and sea level. All crocodiles there disappeared when the Mediterranean dried up about 6 million years ago.
why_it_matters: Re-examining old museum fossils with new tools can reveal species no one knew about. It also shows how changes in temperature and sea level shaped which animals could survive.

background_read: Fossils form when the remains of living things are buried and slowly preserved in rock over very long periods of time.
Scientists name each new species with a two-part scientific name, and they sometimes choose names that honor places, people or legends.
Gavials are a group of crocodiles with long, thin snouts that are good for catching fish.
The Great Sphinx of Giza, a giant statue with a lion's body and a human head, is one of ancient Egypt's most famous monuments and is known for its missing nose.
